title: Accelerating Simulation of Quantum Circuits under Noise via Computational Reuse
problem: Noisy quantum circuit simulation on HPC systems is prohibitively slow because simulators must iteratively re-execute nearly identical circuits thousands of times across different noise model trials, recomputing the same intermediate quantum states from scratch each time.
motivation: Noise-aware simulation is the essential validation tool for quantum algorithm development and error mitigation, yet its iterative nature creates a massive compute bottleneck that limits research throughput.
method: TQSim (Tree-Based Quantum Circuit Simulation) dynamically partitions a quantum circuit into subcircuits and constructs a tree of intermediate results that can be reused across different noisy simulation trials. The system identifies which subcircuit branches diverge due to noise injection and reuses cached intermediate density matrix or statevector results for the converging branches, avoiding redundant re-simulation. The approach is designed for multi-node distributed HPC setups with tight fidelity bounds on the approximation.
key_novelty: Tree-based dynamic partitioning of quantum circuits enables reuse of intermediate quantum state results across noisy simulation trials, reducing total computation proportionally to reuse opportunities.
contributions: TQSim: a tree-based intermediate result reuse framework for noisy quantum circuit simulation
Dynamic circuit partitioning algorithm that identifies reusable subcircuit boundaries under noise
Speedups of up to 3.89x over Qulacs-based baseline simulators for noisy simulation
Multi-node scalable design maintaining tight fidelity bounds

metrics.speedup: up to 3.89x over Qulacs-based noisy simulator baseline

limitations: Not discussed; fidelity bounds and partition granularity trade-offs under high noise rates are not elaborated.
primary_theme: Tree-based intermediate result reuse for noisy quantum circuit simulation
